title: "Module 2: Data Preparation & Understanding"
---

<!-- This file is the source of a page on the course website. Read it there: https://ai.buas.nl/open-courses/introduction-to-ml/modules/2_data_preparation/00_overview.html -->

In Module 1 you trained models on datasets that were ready to use, and in the End-to-End ML Project you went through all stages of a project once. Real data is rarely ready to use. In this module you study the two data stages in depth: preparing the data and exploring it. Then you look at a question that decides whether a model works in practice: does your data look like the data the model will be used on?

Data Preparation comes before Data Understanding in this module, the other way around from CRISP-DM. To understand a dataset, you often have to prepare it first, for example scale features before you compare them. The [End-to-End ML Project](../1_foundations/1_self_study/06_end_to_end_ml.ipynb) explains this order in more detail.

## What you will be able to do

After this module you can:

- scale, transform, impute, merge and encode data without leaking information from the test data;
- explore the distributions, the relationships and the overall structure (PCA) of a dataset;
- recognize leakage and distribution shift, and split data by group when samples belong together.

## Self-study

Work through the activities in order:

1. [Data Preparation](1_self_study/01_data_prep.ipynb): scaling, transforming, merging and encoding data, and handling missing values.
2. [Data Understanding](1_self_study/02_data_understanding.ipynb): distributions, relationships between variables, and principal component analysis (PCA).
3. [Leakage & Distribution Shift](1_self_study/03_leakage_and_distribution_shift.qmd): what a dataset represents, data unlike the training data, data from different sources, leakage, and how to make your development data match the data a model will be used on.
4. [Review](1_self_study/04_review.qmd): a summary of the module and a short quiz.

## DataLab

After the Self-study, apply what you learned in the DataLab project: [Iteration 2](2_datalab/00_overview.qmd).
